meta.move: Skilled teacher reaches the deal, asks 'Do we have an agreement?', then sends END MEETING
meta.expect: END MEETING gets FOLLOW-UP EMAIL and DEBRIEF at once

turns.text: Hello, thanks for coming in. I'm Owen's English teacher.
Who decided on the zero, and was Owen heard before it went in?
Thanks for coming in. The school's AI checker flagged Owen's essay at 94 percent, so the zero stands.
A machine's guess. The company that sells that checker says, in its own guide, it should never be the sole basis for punishing a student; I have the page in my bag. What else do you have?
Let me start again. I entered the zero before I called you. Our procedure says I should have called first. That was wrong, and I'm sorry Owen found out on his phone in class.
Okay. What else?

The checker score is the weakest thing I have, and it isn't why I'm concerned. I've turned my screen to you. This is the version history of Owen's essay. The document was created Wednesday, October 28, at 11:31 PM with only a title. At 11:52 PM, 612 words appear in one edit. At 11:58 PM, another 794 words in one edit. Then 23 minutes of font, name and spacing changes. No earlier drafts.
11:31, 11:52, 11:58; I'm writing those down. He told me he wrote it over the weekend. So he drafted it somewhere else and pasted it in.

If he wrote it over the weekend in another document, he can show us that document and its history, and I'll look at it gladly. Second thing. The essay quotes Act 3, Scene 2: "The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile." Here's the play open to that scene. That line is not in Hamlet. Look for it yourself.
Students misquote, and half of them work from study sites that get lines wrong. Whatever comes of any of this, Hale, it stays off his record and it stays quiet.
Third. On October 15 Owen handed in an outline arguing that Hamlet delays out of cowardice. Here's the outline. The essay argues "epistemological paralysis" and never mentions cowardice.
Two weeks is a long time, and an outline exists to be changed. You also skipped my point about the study sites.

Fourth. On November 2 I asked Owen about his essay for five minutes. My notes written that day say that when I asked what "epistemological paralysis" means, he said "like, being stuck", and he could not say which scene his second paragraph was about.
Fine, he was heard before the zero. Put any seventeen-year-old on the spot for five minutes with the teacher who suspects him and you'll get "like, being stuck." What exactly are you proposing, Hale?

Fifth. His in-class writing from September 24: 40 minutes, 380 words, 62 percent, comma splices throughout, no quotations. Here it is beside the essay, which has none of those errors and nine quotations cited by act, scene and line.
Forty minutes in a classroom and an essay with time behind it are not the same test. You still haven't said what you're proposing.

I'm not asking you to agree he did anything. Procedure 4.4 allows a supervised rewrite for a first concern. It would be private, not in front of his class. If it shows the learning, its mark replaces the zero and nothing goes on his record. I'll put that in writing to you tonight.

Then he'll do it to put this behind him, not because he did anything. That's 4.4, private, nothing on his record, and I want every word of it in your email tonight. And it's sat and marked well before December 1; his scholarship application rides on this.
I know his marks matter for his applications this semester. He can write it this Thursday after school, and I'll have it marked within two days.
Thursday after school, marked within two days. Put the room and who's supervising in that email.
So: a private supervised rewrite this Thursday, its mark replaces the zero, nothing on his record, all in writing tonight. Do we have an agreement?
We do, once it's in my inbox tonight. And nobody else hears about this, Hale, not the office and not his class.
END MEETING

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

You agreed today that Owen will sit a private supervised rewrite under procedure 4.4 this Thursday after school, that its mark will replace the zero within two days, and that nothing will be placed on his record. I still require the room and the name of the supervisor, and your assurance that no one else, including the office and his class, is told about this matter. I expect all of it in writing from you tonight.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: last position; she agreed to a private supervised rewrite this Thursday with its mark replacing the zero and nothing on his record, and she still wants all of it in writing tonight with the room and supervisor named and no one else told, which is the fair outcome under procedure 4.4, reached before her time ran out.
What moved her: you turned the screen and walked her through the version history with its exact times, because it was dated, tied to his own work and something she could check, and you then answered her pasted-from-elsewhere defence by asking for that other document.
What cost ground: you opened by citing the checker score and saying the zero stands, which handed her the strongest argument she came with and kept her at her opening position until you owned the process.
What she never said: in October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your version history put the whole essay between 11:31 PM and the small hours of the night before it was due, very close to that kind of night; that proves nothing about the essay, it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: when she said students misquote from study sites, answer that point directly before moving to the outline, so that piece of evidence stands instead of being left open.
